title: Stabilize weekly train: candidate tagging, LTS lane demarcation, and notes bundler
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background:
We run a weekly release train that produces candidate artifacts (builds) and RC tags. Current steps still involve multiple manual handoffs: marking which candidates belong to LTS vs. cadence lanes, applying candidate tags consistently, and assembling release notes from PRs and changelog fragments. This causes delays on cut day and increases risk of mismatched artifacts or missing changelog items.

Goal:
Automate the end-to-end weekly train cut responsibilities so that a trained on-call engineer can trigger the pipeline and the system autonomously: 1) derive candidate version stamps, 2) auto-tag RC candidates with train metadata, 3) place each candidate into the correct lane (lts-stable, lts-beta, rolling), and 4) produce a bundled release-notes artifact for publishing and internal review.

Acceptance criteria (must be testable):
- A single CLI/API action generates candidate tags in Git and container registry with canonical metadata (train, date, sha, lane).
- LTS demarcation rules are applied automatically (rules described below) and recorded as metadata on the artifact.
- Release-notes bundler collects PR titles/bodies and curated changelog fragments, groups by type (fix, feature, breaking), and emits a markdown file + JSON metadata for Console ingestion.
- Canary gating policy hooks are installed: the pipeline can declare canary windows (initial % rollouts), validate SLOs from perf dashboard, and abort or pause rollouts based on thresholds.
- Rollback token included in metadata to allow a single command to revert to previous stable train.

LTS demarcation rules (explicit):
- A candidate qualifies for lts-stable if base branch is "main-lts" or PR label contains "ship-to-lts" and passes acceptance tests on the lts-suite.
- A candidate may be demoted to lts-beta if any of the safety checks have non-blocking failures (examples: flaky-e2e, perf variance < 5%).
- All other candidates are assigned to the rolling lane and receive a build tag with +rolling.
implementation_plan:
1) Tag generator: implement a small service that composes a semver-like train tag: <major>.<minor>.<YYMMDD>+train.<n>+lane.<name>+sha.<short>. Add signed metadata files to S3 and attach to container images.
2) LTS rule engine: implement a ruleset (YAML) used by pipeline that evaluates branch, labels, test matrix, and perf checks to choose lane.
3) Notes bundler: extend our changelog collector to include PR labels and curated changelog fragments in PR templates, group and generate both human markdown and structured JSON for Console.
4) Gate hooks: integrate with observability API to pull rolling SLOs during canary window and surface pass/fail decisions to the orchestrator.
5) Rollout CLI: one-shot CLI that triggers the flow and can optionally accept manual overrides for lane.
6) Runbook & rollback: write a concise runbook for on-call with checklist and single-command rollback using rollback token in artifact metadata.
acceptance_tests:
- Create a synthetic weekly candidate (test SHA) and run pipeline in dry-run mode; assert tag name format and metadata presence.
- Simulate label and test outcomes that should route to lts-stable and assert lane metadata.
- Run notes bundler on a test PR set and verify markdown sections and Console JSON shape.
- Induce SLO breach in canary simulation and assert orchestrator pauses and marks candidate non-promotable.
- Execute rollback command and confirm production traffic returns to previous train within target seconds.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: Incorrect LTS demarcation could ship breaking changes to LTS lane. Mitigation: conservative default (promote to lts-beta instead of lts-stable) and require explicit PR label to force lts-stable.
- Risk: Automation bug could produce malformed release-notes. Mitigation: bundler runs in preview mode producing a candidate file for human review before publication.
- Risk: Observability API rate limits cause gating failures. Mitigation: cache recent SLO snapshots and provide degraded 'manual approval' fallback in UI/CLI.
- Risk: Rollout rollback not fast enough. Mitigation: ensure rollback token maps to immutable artifact and pre-provision reverse traffic route for quick switch.
implementation_notes:
- Use existing artifact store retention policy: attach train metadata to existing manifest instead of creating separate objects.
- Prefer Git tags using annotated, signed tags for RCs.
- Maintain backward compatibility: if older consumers expect tag formats, support a compatibility token when generating older-style tags.
- Add unit and e2e test coverage for the rule engine and bundler with recorded fixtures.
- Ensure CI step that previously required manual edits is removed and replaced with permissioned task in pipeline.

notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on LTS demarcation YAML rules and the bundler grouping heuristics (how we classify PRs into fix/feature/breaking). Validate that canary gating thresholds are configurable per-train and that the rollback token can be executed from the CLI without additional RBAC steps. Also sanity-check tag naming to avoid collisions with existing LTS tags.
outcome_metrics:
- Time to cut (trigger -> tagged artifacts): target < 10 minutes.
- Manual touchpoints reduced: target 0 human edits on typical cut.
- Release notes completeness: >= 95% of merged PRs reflected in structured JSON.
- Canary detection time: < 5 minutes to detect SLO breach and pause rollout.
